_comment: Dark-slab product captions, for a screen recording rather than a social short. Four deliberate departures from red-card.json, which was measured off a news-style channel and reads as a chyron: (1) the slab is near-black at 12% transparency instead of saturated -- a screen demo is already a busy, mostly-white frame, and a coloured bar competes with the very UI the video is pointing at, while a dark one recedes behind it; (2) sentence case, not uppercase -- a tutorial that shouts is a tutorial nobody finishes, and mixed case carries word shape, which is what makes a line readable at a glance; (3) the spotlight is the same accent as config/cards/brands/mint.json and the lower third, so captions, a name label and an end card on one film read as one channel; (4) narrower lines and fewer words per group, because the frame under them is content the viewer needs to see. dark-card-uk.json is this preset widened for Cyrillic.

emphasis._comment: The talk's main points, named per video in an --emphasis-file and marked for the whole life of their card. A DIFFERENT hue from states.active on purpose: the active colour is already the moving spotlight, so reusing it would make 'this is the point' and 'this is the word being said' the same signal and neither would read.

overlays._note: Colour of the SOURCE video's own lower-third graphics to dodge, not the colour of this card. A screencast has none, so there is nothing to dodge.

_geometry.target: 1280x720 screen recording with a round webcam bubble in the bottom-left corner
_geometry.why_bottom_margin_96: 96 on the 1920 canvas scales to 64px at 720p, which puts the card's baseline clear of the Windows taskbar (top edge ~y 682) without pushing it up into the page content.
_geometry.why_max_line_1080: 1080 on the 1920 canvas scales to 720px at 720p, centred on x=640, so the card spans x 280..1000 and never reaches the webcam bubble at x<190. Widening this past ~1150 makes them collide.
